info.text:
A free car from a game show can come with a tax bill in the thousands.
The IRS counts prizes as income at fair market value, and the show reports it on Form 1099-MISC.
Our math: a $30,000 car all taxed at 22% means $6,600 in federal tax, before state tax, sales tax, registration and insurance.
In 2004, Oprah's $28,500 free cars came with tax bills of up to $7,000 (CNN/Money).
You can usually refuse a prize, and a refused prize isn't income (IRS Pub 525).
Sources: IRS Publication 525, CNN/Money (2004), IRS tax brackets.
News and education, not financial advice.
